qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant Dutch banking oligopoly (ABN AMRO, ING, Rabobank) commanding deep domestic deposit franchises and primary-bank switching barriers. However, mortgages face competition from institutional pension platforms, and compliance/KYC remediation costs have historically eroded operating leverage.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). ABN AMRO operates an entrenched oligopoly retail and commercial franchise in the Netherlands with sticky primary-bank deposits, but is constrained by commercial banking's high structural fade rate (Tier 4 CAP). Cyclical peak net interest income is normalizing downward with ECB rate cuts, while non-bank mortgage platforms and digital challengers continuously pressure lending spreads and payment fees.
qualitative.evidence: ABN AMRO generates ~90% of operating profit domestically in Northwest Europe, holding top-three positions in Dutch mortgages, SME lending, and consumer deposits. 10-year historical ROE has averaged ~8.2%, reflecting severe compression during negative-rate years (ROE was 5.3% in 2021) before rebounding to ~11% in 2023. High compliance overhead and domestic rate sensitivity limit sustainable multi-decade competitive longevity.
